html:
Olympias was a princess of Epirus, a wife of Philip II of Macedon and the mother of Alexander the Great. She lived from about 375 to 316 BCE and fought hard for power in Macedon after both men were gone.

She was the daughter of a king of the Molossians in Epirus and married Philip around 357 BCE. Ancient writers, mostly hostile, describe her as fierce, proud and devoted to the wild rites of Dionysus, even keeping snakes. Her marriage broke down when Philip took a new Macedonian wife. After Philip's murder in 336 BCE, Olympias had that wife and her baby killed, and some suspected her of a hand in the murder itself.

While Alexander was away conquering Persia, she sent him letters full of complaints about his regent in Macedon, Antipater. After Alexander's death in 323 BCE she joined the wars between his generals. In 317 BCE she had Alexander's half brother, King Philip III, put to death. Then Cassander besieged her in Pydna, and after it fell she was killed in 316 BCE by relatives of people she had executed.
sum: Olympias was a princess of Epirus, a wife of Philip II of Macedon and the mother of Alexander the Great. She lived from about 375 to 316 BCE and fought hard for power in Macedon after both men were gone.
